RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests a minute this operation allows the caller (the key or the signed-in person; the address for a call without a credential), for the most restrictive limit the request was counted against.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left before that limit answers `429 rate_limited`: slow down before it reaches 0.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the limit's current window ends.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before sending the request again: on a `429 rate_limited` from the per-minute request limit, and on a `503 unavailable` (the service is waking). The SDKs wait this long before they retry.

X-Request-Id.description: The request's id, also `requestId` in an error body: what support asks for. A request's own `X-Request-Id` (8 to 64 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`) is kept, so your logs and ours share it; otherwise a new one is made.

RateLimited.description: `rate_limited`: too many requests. Wait `Retry-After` seconds and send it again (the SDKs retry it for you). Unavailable.description: `unavailable`: the service is waking or briefly cannot reach its database or storage. Send it again after `Retry-After` seconds; the SDKs do when that is safe (`GET`, `HEAD`, `DELETE`, or a call with an `Idempotency-Key`).

Options update during a realtime session; fields left out are unchanged.
`latencyMode` switches the decode model policy from the
next engine step on. `spokenLanguage` changes the transcription language
from the next engine step (`""` or `"auto"` = auto-detect; an
unsupported code is ignored). `speakerLabels` turns speaker
labelling on (`on` or `auto`) or off (`off`) from the next engine step —
enabling labels speakers from that point; earlier segments are not
re-attributed. `translate` replaces the whole target-language list
(subject to the same cap as at creation); `[]` turns
translation off. Already-delivered segments and settled sentences
are not re-transcribed or re-translated.

voice.description:
Replace the spoken list — languages or `lang:voice` pairs
(see `SessionOptions::voice`).

voiceByLang.description:
Replace the whole per-language voice map (see
`SessionOptions::voiceByLang`); `{}` clears every pin.

oneOf.description:
Capture clock heartbeat (live sources): `pcm` = cumulative samples
the client captured (16kHz-equivalent), `wall` = its monotonic
seconds since capture start (excluding system sleep).  Lets the
server detect capture loss and keep the timeline honest; optional
and backward compatible.

ClientMessages.description: Copy overrides; `null` keeps the app's own.

deprecatedBelow.description:
Versions below this one are deprecated: they work, without the newer
features.  `null`: none are.

latest.description: The newest build; `null` when there is none to offer.

message.description: Copy that replaces the app's own for these states.

unsupportedBelow.description:
Versions below this one are unsupported: the app blocks until it is
updated (only when `latest` is newer).  `null`: none are.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file, lowercase hex.

signature.description:
Ed25519 over the file by the app's release key, base64.  The app
installs nothing whose signature does not verify.

url.description:
Where to download the build: https, no credential, never moved to
another version.

catchup.description:
`true` when the segment was decoded by the fast model: the `auto`
transcription method catching up after falling behind real time, or
the `fast` method. Absent when the accurate model decoded it.

confidence.description: Segment-level recognition confidence, 0..1 (mean of word probs).

decoder.description:
Which model decoded this segment (`fast` or `accuracy`).
Always present on current servers; optional only for
wire compatibility.  `catchup` is the same signal as a boolean.

gapBefore.description:
Seconds of capture audio the CLIENT reported lost immediately
before this segment (from `{"op":"clock"}` heartbeat accounting).
The words spoken in that span never reached the engine. Absent
when no loss was detected.

language.description:
Language this segment was transcribed in (detected or forced),
as a whisper language code, when known.

latencyS.description:
Emit latency in seconds (wall clock at emit minus segment end on the
audio timeline): how far behind the speaker this line was COMMITTED.
A line a correction pass then holds (a doubted word's re-decode, the
language model's reading) gets a `transcript.latency` frame when the
hold releases, with the time to its FINAL text — the figure to keep.
It does NOT include the sentence closing, the translation, delivery
or render — a reader waiting on a translated line waits longer, and
`SentenceView.translationLatencyS` is the figure for that.

Only present on live-input realtime sessions, and absent for a line the two
clocks cannot be compared for — audio that arrived faster than
realtime puts a line's end ahead of the wall clock. Absent means
"not measured"; it is never reported as 0 for unknown.

recognizedText.description:
When the recording follows a script and the engine took the
script's words for some of this segment's (beyond case and
punctuation): what the recognizer heard before it did.  `text` is
what the reader sees; the segment's voice (voice clips, voice
tracks, the live voice) says `text` only when the audio supports
every word of it, and this otherwise.  Absent when `text` is the
recognizer's own.

scriptFrom.description:
When this segment matched the script: the first script word it
read, so `scriptFrom..scriptPos` is the stretch of script it covers.
Absent when it did not match (an aside, a held line).

scriptPos.description:
When the recording follows a script (`Recording.script`): how many
of the script's words the engine has matched up to and including
this segment — where the teleprompter stands.  Words are the
script's whitespace-separated tokens that carry a letter or digit.
Absent without a script.

speakerConfidence.description:
Diarization confidence that the segment belongs to `speaker`, 0..1:
how clearly the segment's voice matches that speaker rather than any
other tracked speaker. Absent without diarization.

speakerProvisional.description:
`true` while the speaker label is tentative (low diarization
confidence): a later `transcript.speaker` frame settles it, possibly
after a `transcript.amended` that moved it. Absent when final.

translationSources.description: Where each language's translation came from: "cache", "google" or "llm".

ConfidencePolicy.description: Env defaults, overridden per broadcast, transcription or recording.

hideBelow.description:
A line scoring below this is hidden as "Audio unclear".  The
score is the line's own confidence — the mean of its word
probabilities — so this is the one number that decides the gap.
0..1; the default is 0.60.

lowThreshold.description: Words with `prob` below this are *low confidence*.

suppressCount.description:
This many low-confidence words suppress a line for listeners.

**No longer read.**  Suppression is `hide_below` — the line's own
score — since 2026-09-12; the field is kept so settings carrying it
still round-trip rather than being rejected.

voiced.description:
Whether this correction's line is voiced (voice clips and voice
tracks) as corrected, decided when the correction was applied.
Present on a word or line correction that stands; absent on a
speaker name and on a reverted correction. `false` means the
corrected text has words the audio does not support: the
transcript, reading and export show it, but the line is voiced from
what the recognizer heard (`notVoicedReason` says why).

lines.description: Whole-line rewrites, applied in the same batch after `edits`.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last.

What the key is for, shown in the VocalStack app beside it (e.g.
"OBS on the studio PC"): at most 100 characters.

Creator-chosen, globally unique (#3, #5).  Derived from `name` when
omitted.  It can be changed later (`PATCH`).

source.description:
`{kind:"mic"}` (default) or `{kind:"stream", url}`: audio the server

A top-up: any whole-cent amount inside `GET /v1/billing/plans`'s
`topUpRange` (its `topUpAmounts` are the presets).

A promo code (`POST /v1/billing/promo-codes/check` tells what it

subscription's first payment.  `404 promo_code_invalid` when it

Deprecated and ignored: `acceptTerms` is the one consent.  It covers
the Terms and the customer's request that the purchase start now;
no withdrawal waiver is asked (a consumer cannot waive it in advance
for a service).  Still accepted, so older clients that send it keep

CreateLiveTranscription.description:
`POST /v1/transcriptions/live`: a transcription captured as it is
spoken — this device's microphone, or a stream the server pulls.
It is created idle; `POST /v1/transcriptions/{id}/recordings` starts it.

broadcasts.description: Broadcasts (their ids) to feed from the start.

allowDownload.description: Both default to on (design: "on by default and can be turned off per link").

allowTranslate.description:
Design 24's `k.tr`: may this link be read (and heard) translated?
Defaults to `DEFAULT_ALLOW_TRANSLATE` — on, so a link keeps doing
what share links have always done; the owner turns it off per link
when they want to stop paying the provider for that link.

label.description: Who the link is for ("Board pack — Nadia").

color.description: One of the eight colours; the first no tag has yet when omitted.

name.description: 1 to 40 characters, unique in the account however it is cased.

CreateTranscription.description:
`POST /v1/transcriptions`: JSON for a URL, or the `options` part of a
multipart upload whose `file` part carries the media.

Design 57's crop step: once the source is stored and measured the
job waits in `cropping` (with `peaks` for a waveform) until
`POST /v1/recordings/{id}/job/start` names the window to
transcribe.  Default false: transcribe the whole file right away.

durationS.description:
The source's length as the browser measured it, kept for the list
and the reader until the engine reads its own.

name.description: Display name; the file name or the URL when omitted.

shareLink.description:
Whether the transcription is created with its default share link
(download, export and translation on).  Opt-in (2026-10-20): absent
or `false` creates none, and links are added later with
`POST /v1/transcriptions/{id}/share-links`; the dashboard asks for it.

startS.description:
The window to transcribe, when it was chosen before the job was
created: an upload is trimmed in the browser on the host's own copy
and sent only at Start (Alex, 2026-10-02), so it arrives already
cropped.  Not with `crop`.  Absent = from the start / to the end.

url.description: Fetched server-side.  Absent for a file upload.

CreatedAppStreamKey.description: The answer that made an app stream key: the one time it is in full.

maskedStreamKey.description: The key as it is shown afterwards, e.g. `vs_rtmp_…k7xq`.

serverUrl.description: The encoder's server URL, as `GET /v1/rtmp` gives it.

streamKey.description:
The key in full, to paste into the encoder (or set in it): only in
this answer.  It is kept as a hash; a lost key is deleted and a new
one made.

CropRange.description: A window of a file, in seconds into it.  `end_s` absent = to the end.

CropWindow.description: A window of the source, in seconds into it.  `end_s` absent = to the end.

CurrentRecording.description:
The recording in flight (`currentRecording`): on a transcription, its
open recording; on a broadcast, the open recording
of a live transcription feeding it, which is what its listeners are sent.

transcriptionId.description:
On a broadcast's: the live transcription it is being made in (one
of `Broadcast.transcriptions`).

Decoder.description: Which model actually decoded a committed segment.

oneOf.description:
The fast model: the `fast` method, or the `auto` method
catching up after falling behind real time.
The accurate model.

DowngradeKeepDays.description: The account's days data is kept after a downgrade (Terms §14).

days.description:
The days in force for this account: the most generous of the
setting and what a lowering's notice protects for it.

lowering.description: A lowering the account was told of, not applied yet; null otherwise.

oneOf.description:
A realtime session's token passed its connect-by deadline
(`expiresAt`): create a new realtime session.

The engine serving an open realtime socket went away mid-stream (its
machine stopped or crashed) and no other engine could carry the
stream on: what was committed before stays, nothing after it was
transcribed.  Sent as an `error` frame just before the socket
closes (1011), and what the SDKs report when the socket closes
with neither `session.done` nor an `error` frame.  Retryable: open
a new realtime session (a recording: start again) to go on.
The authenticated actor may not act on this resource.

The broadcast exists but its host archived it: the link is retired,
and that is a different thing from a link that was never real.
Design 43 says so to whoever pasted it, because "no broadcast found"
sends them to check a code that was perfectly correct.
No such broadcast / transcription / recording / correction, or it is archived.

A uniqueness or concurrency conflict: code taken, already
recording on another device.

The action is not valid from the resource's current state, e.g.
stop on a live (not paused) recording, correct an unsettled line.
A private broadcast: exchange the password for a listener token.
An abuse control fired; retry later.

A preview is being rendered right now: the ask started it, the
render files the clip, and the next ask is a cache hit.  Answered
`202 Accepted`, not `503` — the engine is not unavailable, the clip
is simply not finished, and saying "service unavailable" about a
perfectly healthy first play puts a red line in the caller's
console and sends people looking for a fault that is not there.

Nothing on this deployment can speak the language that was asked
for: no voice asset for it in the bucket, or no preview line
written for it.  Permanent as far as the caller is concerned —
this is what `preview_pending` must never be used to say, because
a client polling for something that is not coming eventually tells
somebody to try again in a moment, forever.

The account or API key was suspended by an administrator (a kill
switch, reversible; a revoked key is `invalid_token`).  Retrying
does not help; contacting support does.

The API key passed its expiry (`expiresInDays` at creation, or the
24 h grace after a rotation).  Use its replacement or mint a new one.
The API key was revoked.  Final: mint a new key.

An API key was sent from a web page (the request carries a browser
`Origin`).  Keys are for servers: keep the key on your server and
have your page call your server.  The API offers no browser
credential for keys; a person signed in to VocalStack itself uses
their own access token.

The account has not enough credit (HTTP 402): the balance is at or
below zero, at or below what a new transcription's minimum costs
(`rates.minimumSeconds` at its rate; for a batch's start, the larger
of that and `rates.batchFileMinimumSeconds` for each of its files),
or below the cost of a file of known length.  `data.details` carries
`balance`, `currency` (`usd`), `plan`, `topUpUrl`, and `required`
when the cost is known up front (that minimum, or the file's cost).  Not retryable until
credit is added.

The API key reached its usage cap (HTTP 402): what it may spend in
total or per month, week or day (UTC), set by the account when the
key was made.  New transcriptions with the key are refused, and its
live recordings and realtime sessions stop; the account's other keys
keep working.  `data.details` carries `apiKeyId`, `cap`, `period`
(`lifetime`, `month`, `week`, `day`), `used`, `resetsAt` (null for
`lifetime`), and `required` when a file's cost would pass the cap.
Not retryable until the period resets or the cap is raised.

Auto top-up and the customer portal need a saved payment method,
and the account has made no payment yet (HTTP 409).  Make a
payment (a top-up or a subscription) first.

The signed-in person, or the account an API key belongs to, has not
accepted the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy that took effect
with the billing update of October 2026 (HTTP 403).  Until someone
accepts them in the Dashboard (an organisation's keys work once one
of its owners or administrators has), calls that start paid work or
commit the account further, and every API key call, are refused;
cancelling, turning auto top-up off, the customer portal, refund
requests and account deletion still work.  `data.details` carries
`termsVersion`, `privacyVersion` and `acceptUrl`.

The payment method pays for an active subscription and cannot be
removed (HTTP 409).  Add another method and make it the default
first (`POST /v1/billing/payment-methods/manage`).

The payment provider needs a billing name and address before it can
make this invoice or receipt (HTTP 409).  Save the invoice details
(`PUT /v1/billing/details`) and ask again.

The promo code does not exist, has expired, is used up, was already
redeemed by this account, or does not apply to this purchase (HTTP
404).

Auto top-up is off for this account (HTTP 409): turn it on with
`PUT /v1/billing/auto-top-up` first.

A date range is longer than the route allows (HTTP 400):
`GET /v1/billing/usage` takes at most 92 days.

A plan limit is used up (HTTP 402): `concurrent_transcriptions`
(realtime sessions, live recordings and running jobs at once).
`data.details` carries `metric`, `limit`, `used`, `resetsAt` (null
for a concurrency limit, which frees up as they finish), `plan` and
`topUpUrl`.

The `Idempotency-Key` was already used, in the last 24 hours, for a
different request (another route or another body) (HTTP 422).  Use a
fresh key for a new request.

No route has this method: the path exists, the method does not
(HTTP 405).  The `Allow` header lists the methods it takes.
The request body is over the route's size cap (HTTP 413).

The body's `Content-Type` is not one the route reads (HTTP 415);
JSON routes need `application/json`.

The JSON body parsed but does not match the route's schema: a
missing field or a wrong type (HTTP 422).  The message names it.

The request ran past its route's time cap (HTTP 504).  Retrying
may succeed; long work belongs in the async (file) routes.

The service is starting up or briefly cannot reach its database
(HTTP 503, with `Retry-After`).  Nothing was wrong with the
request: send it again after `Retry-After` seconds.

details.description:
Error-specific detail: `conflict` on broadcast creation carries
`{ suggestions: [...] }`; `conflict` on recording start carries
`{ recordingId, takeover: true }`.

Fix.description: One word-level correction inside a `transcript.amended` frame.

kind.description:
Which engine pass produced it, namespaced `amend:<mechanism>`:
`amend:redo:doubt` (doubted words re-decoded), `amend:redo:span`
(doubted span re-decoded whole), `amend:redo:vote` (two consecutive
re-decodes agreed on a different word), `amend:redo:insert`,
`amend:redo:tail` (word across the step cut; `repl` empty = dropped),

gets `suppressed` and no text, everyone who is shown the text — the
host, and a share-link reader — gets `unclear` and all of it. Set by
the relay, which is the only place that knows the rule: the floor is
a per-recording setting over a deployment default, so a client
applying its own number would mark a different set of lines from the
ones its audience is missing.

It is also what tells a reader NOT to ask for the line's audio: a
hidden line is spoken to nobody, the owner included, and the clip
route answers 404 for it.

from the end of this line's speech to the translation being attached
(how far the translation trails the speaker).

It measured from the sentence CLOSING until 2026-09-12, which is a
late leg of the pipeline and omitted everything before it, including
the close wait — it read 2.6 s where a listener had waited 10.6 s.
This is the whole wait, and it is the number to show a reader asking
how far behind they are.

Present on definitive translations of live input only; a file job
transcodes faster than realtime and has no speaker to be behind.

oneOf.description: Still growing; `text` may change and `seqs` may extend.
Complete. `text` changes only if one of its segments is amended.
Its segments were regrouped into a neighbouring sentence; discard.

A heartbeat while the machine gets ready (`stage`: `download`, then
`model`); each one re-arms the client's ready deadline.  Send no
audio yet.
The realtime session is ready: send audio from now on.

One final segment, with word timings, numbered by `seq` (0, 1, 2…,
gapless).  Append it; the draft tail it covers is gone.  Its text or
speaker can later be corrected in place by `transcript.amended`.

The live tail: the words heard since the last commit, still
changing.  A full replacement of the previous draft: redraw the tail
with `segments`, never append it.  It begins where the last committed
segment ended; an empty list clears it.  Live input only (a file
sends none unless `events.drafts` asks), and never to a recording's
subscribers.

Word timings for the live tail as they firm up (`events.words`);
ephemeral, carries no `seq`.

An already-delivered committed segment was rewritten by the engine
(a later decode with more context corrected a word, punctuation or
the speaker). `text` is the segment's full new text.

The segment's language from now on, when the amend read it again
in another one (a hand-back to Whisper rewriting what the English
model wrote for it); absent when unchanged.

Words of the new text the script wrote (a misheard word the
rescorer swapped for a near-identical script word), by position
in `text`'s words; they take `Word.script`.  Absent when none.

tail.description:
When the amend rewrote the segment's last words: they replace

oneOf.description:
A delivered segment's latency, measured again now that the engine's
correction passes are done with it.  `latencyS` is the figure from
`CommittedSegment.latencyS` plus the time the segment then spent
under a hold (a doubted word's re-decode, the language model's
reading): how far behind the speaker this line was FINAL, which is
what the harness's μ Lat counts (a doubted row at its settle time).
Replaces the segment's `latencyS`.  Sent only for a line a hold was
on, and only on live input (a realtime session, never a file); a
line no pass held keeps the latency its commit carried.

A tentative speaker label on a delivered segment was settled:
`verdict` is "confirmed" (later evidence agrees), "amended" (the
segment was re-attributed; the `transcript.amended` frame with the
new speaker precedes this) or "unverified" (no better evidence
arrived, the label stands). `speaker`/`speakerConfidence` are the
segment's current values; `speakerProvisional` is now false.

A speaker's gender, as the pitch band heard it, once it settles
(`casting::roster`).  Sent once per speaker per realtime session (or recording) — twice
only if a verdict changes as more of their audio arrives.

`gender` is `"male"` or `"female"`; a speaker the band refuses to
judge is never the subject of this frame at all, because "not
known" is not a verdict to publish.  `confidence` is the share of
their pitch that backs it.

What it is FOR: the voice sheet marks a speaker's chip with it and
opens the group of voices that suits them.  It is deliberately not
used to pick a voice — that is `voice_cast`'s job, on the engine,
where the verdict comes from.

A diarized speaker turned out to be somebody the caller has a
saved voice for (`speaker_id`).  Sent the moment the match lands,
which is a few seconds into that person talking — never with the
first row, because a second of audio is not enough to put a name
to and a wrong name is worse than none.

So a transcript reads "Speaker 2" for a line or two and then
becomes "Marcus Reed", retroactively, for every row already shown.
Clients are expected to re-label what they have rather than only
what arrives next — that is the whole shape of this frame.

An empty `name` withdraws a claim: the end of a realtime session re-decides
the whole room at once with more of everybody, and it can take a
name back as well as give one.  `voiceId` is the saved voice that
recognised them.  `confidence` is a cosine similarity, not a
probability — comparable between speakers, not a percentage.

`tone` marks a name that came from a clone's tone colour instead
of a verification embedding: weaker evidence, and worth showing
differently if a client shows it at all.

color.description:
The colour this person reads in, as the caller stated it in
`identifyVoices` — a palette slot `"1"`–`"6"` or `"#rrggbb"`.

oneOf.description:
Full-replacement upsert of one sentence, keyed by `sentenceId`.
Sent whenever the sentence grows, changes, closes, or gains a
translation. Only with `sentences.enabled`.

sources.description: Where each language's translation came from: "cache", "google" or "llm".

oneOf.description:
A spoken rendering of one definitive sentence (`SessionOptions::voice`).
The engine sends the clip inline (`audio`, base64 Ogg/Opus, 24 kHz
mono); the API stores it and replaces `audio` with `url`
(`/v1/recordings/{id}/voice/{sentenceId}?lang=…`, `&format=caf` for
Apple) before relaying.  `latencyS` is sentence close → clip ready.

cloned.description:
True when `voice` names a cloned voice: the listener must be
told the speech is synthetic and whose it imitates.

part.description:
Which piece of the line this clip is, and how many pieces the
line was spoken in (`tts::split`).  A long line is cut at its
clause boundaries so the first piece can be heard while the
rest are still being made; the pieces are played back to back
and are ONE line on screen, with one id and one translation.
`0` and `1` for a line spoken whole, which is most of them.

queueWaitS.description:
How long the clip waited for a synthesis slot before any work
on it started. `synth_s` alone cannot tell an engine that is
slow from an engine that is BUSY, and those want opposite
fixes: a slow one wants a smaller model, a busy one wants more
lanes. In the tail of a backed-up realtime session every clip has a
small `synthS` and a large one of these.

speakerToAudioS.description:
The one honest clock: how long after the speaker finished
saying this line did audio of it exist.

Every other latency here measures one leg, and they start and
end in different places, so none of them can be added to
another and all of them flatter the system. This measures the
whole journey — decode, close, settle, translate, queue,
synthesis — because that is the only one anybody hears.

synthS.description: Synthesis wall time, seconds — the work, not the waiting.

voice.description:
The voice that spoke it, by its catalogue id (`GET
/v1/voices/available`) — or `clone:<id>` for a cloned voice.
Absent only on frames from before the engine reported it.

voiceKey.description:
Which audience choice this clip was made for: the voice half
of the `SessionOptions::voice` entry behind it, empty (and
absent on the wire) for "the engine's default".  `voice` says
what spoke; this says what was *asked for*, and it is what a
subscriber's `?voice=` is matched against — the two differ
whenever the asker named no voice.

oneOf.description:
Why a listener who picked a voice is not hearing it yet — or will
not hear it at all.  Sent once per (language, voice) and state,
and filtered to the listeners on that pair exactly as
`transcript.voice` is.

Before this a listener who picked a voice whose assets were not on
the machine got silence and a server log line: the sentences went
by unspoken and nothing said why.  `preparing` means the assets
are being fetched and the clips will follow (the engine holds each
sentence for them rather than dropping it); `unavailable` means
this voice cannot be had here, and `detail` says why in the
engine's own words.

detail.description: What is being fetched, or why it cannot be had.

voiceKey.description:
The audience choice this is about — the same value
`transcript.voice.voiceKey` carries, empty for the engine's
default.

oneOf.description:
A stream pinned to a spoken language: whether the speech is that
language.  Not an error: the stream goes on in the language it was
given.  `mismatch` follows 30 s or more of another language within
a few minutes and clears (`matches`) after about two minutes of the
pinned one; `unknown` until either is clear.  `change_unsupported`:
a change of the spoken language this stream could not take; it goes
on in `expected`.  Sent on a change only, to the stream's own socket
and the host's subscription, never to listeners.

fromMediaS.description: Media seconds where the other language began (`mismatch`).

oneOf.description:
Committed rows taken back: the speech there was another language
than the engine that wrote them could read, and another engine is
transcribing it again; its rows follow, under these `seq`s again or
new ones.  Drop them wherever they are shown.

fromMediaS.description: Media seconds from which the transcript is being redone.

oneOf.description:
Text held back (`held`): from `fromMediaS` the speech may be
another language than the engine reads, and its rows wait until
that is known; show a placeholder there.  Then (`held: false`) the
rows went out after all (`outcome` `released`), another engine
writes that span again and its rows follow (`moved`), or it is read
again once the recording ends (`untranscribed`).

language.description: The language heard there, when known.

oneOf.description:
`input.kind = "stream"`: how the engine's pull of the stream is
going.  Sent on every change of state and every few seconds while
streaming (the counters move).

bytesIn.description: Bytes read from the source and seconds of audio decoded, this run.

detected.description: What the source turned out to be ("HLS · AAC-LC 22.05 kHz …").

error.description: Why the last connection failed or dropped.

programAtMs.description:
Wall clock (ms) of media second 0, when the playlist says
(`EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME`).

sequenceOffsetMs.description:
How far into the broadcast media second 0 is (ms), when the
playlist's numbering says (a YouTube live).

oneOf.description:
`input.prepare`: the source on its way in.  `phase` "fetching"
counts bytes, "extracting" media seconds decoded.
`input.prepare`: the source is stored and ready to transcribe.

durationS.description: The media's length, when it could be read.

peaks.description: The waveform for the trim step (0..1), when the recording waits for one.

identifyVoices.description:
Voices the realtime session may recognise its speakers as.

Diarization says *that* two people are different, never who they
are.  Give it the saved voices belonging to whoever is in the
room and it can say: each one carries a speaker embedding, the
realtime session takes the same embedding off every speaker it hears, and a
match becomes a `transcript.speakerIdentified` frame.

Empty (the default) means nobody is recognised and no such frame
is ever sent.  It is deliberately an explicit list and not "all
the caller's voices": one server holds many realtime sessions at once, and
the set of people who might be in THIS room is the caller's to
state.

Needs `speakerLabels` on — with one speaker there is nobody to tell
apart — and costs nothing on a realtime session that leaves it empty.

latencyMode.description:
Which model transcribes: `auto` (default) runs the accurate model
and switches to the fast one only while the realtime session lags behind
real time; `fast` always uses the fast model (lower latency, lower
accuracy on noisy or non-English audio); `accuracy` never switches.

sentences.description:
Sentence assembly over committed segments. When enabled the realtime session
also emits `transcript.sentence` upserts, and `translate` applies to
whole sentences instead of individual committed segments.

speakerLabels.description:
Speaker labels: `off` (default), `on`, or `auto` (diarized like
`on`; a client that shows labels waits for a second speaker).

spokenLanguage.description: Whisper language code of the speech; absent = auto-detect.

translate.description:
Target languages for async translation of committed segments.
Each commit is followed (later) by a `transcript.translated` frame
referencing its `seq`. Empty = translations disabled.

voice.description:
What to speak: each definitive translated sentence in one of these
languages (or the original sentence when its own language is
listed) is synthesised and delivered as a `transcript.voice`
frame.  Requires `sentences`.  Empty = no speech.

An entry is `"<lang>"` — speak it in whatever voice the engine
picks (`voiceByLang`, else its default) — or `"<lang>:<voice>"`,
naming the voice outright.  The same language may appear several
times with different voices, and each is synthesised once, however
many listeners asked for it: this list is the union of what the
audience chose, and it is what keeps a clip from being rendered
per listener.  `"es"` and `"es:F3"` are different entries and cost
two syntheses, so a caller that means the default says only `"es"`.

voiceByLang.description:
Which voice speaks each language in `voice` (`{"es": "F3"}`), by
the engine's own voice name.  A language absent from the map gets
the engine's default for it — and the clip says which that was.

voiceCast.description:
Cast a distinct, gender-matched voice to each diarized speaker
(default **on**).

The listener still picks one voice per language; with this on it
becomes the voice of the first speaker of its own gender, and
everybody else in the room is cast around it from the same
engine's catalogue — so two men are read in two male voices and a
woman in a female one, without anyone configuring anything.

Off means the listener's pick reads every speaker, which is what
happened before this existed.  It is also what a caller wants when
the choice is editorial rather than practical: a single narrator
for the whole room.

Needs `speakerLabels` on to do anything — with one speaker there is
nothing to cast — and never delays a clip: a speaker whose gender
has not settled yet is read in the listener's pick and moves to
their own voice once it does (see `casting`).

acceptTerms.description: The Terms were accepted for the switch (required).

expectedPrice.description:
The price `GET /v1/billing` showed for the interval
(`subscription.switchPrices`): `409 invalid_state` when it no longer
matches (a version applied in between).

noNewWithdrawalPeriodShown.description:
The customer was shown that a switch starts no new 14-day
withdrawal period: the next renewal is not withdrawable (required).

SettingLowering.description:
A lowering of a billing setting that changes the account's terms (the
days data is kept after a downgrade, the auto top-up daily limit),
told with at least 30 days' notice (docs/billing-price-changes.md §6).

afterDate.description:
Pay as you go: it applies after this date (UTC, `YYYY-MM-DD`); null
for a subscriber.

appliesAt.description:
When it applies to this account (RFC 3339): 00:00 UTC on the day
after `afterDate` on pay as you go; a subscriber's renewal, on or
about that moment.

refundDeadline.description:
The last day to ask for unused paid top-up credit back because of
this lowering (`YYYY-MM-DD`, until 23:59 UTC).

refundWindowOpen.description: Whether that refund window is still open.

renewalOn.description:
A subscriber: from the renewal on or about this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`);
null on pay as you go.

Settings.description:
A broadcast's, transcription's or recording's capture settings (the
design's settings sheet): what a recording made in it starts with.

maxPauseS.description: A paused recording auto-ends after this long.

silenceAutoPauseS.description:
Auto-pause after this much continuous silence (seconds,
≥ 120); absent = the server default (`SILENCE_AUTO_PAUSE_S`, 0 = off).

speakerLabels.description:
Separate the transcript by who is talking (#39: `off` by default):
`auto` and `on` diarize, `auto` labels lines once a second speaker
has been heard.

summary.description:
The language model's summary of a finished recording.  Opt-in
(2026-10-20): off unless asked for; the dashboard asks.  Never for
a recording under a minute (`SHORT_RECORDING_S`).

summaryTranslations.description:
The summary and title translated into each language the audience
used (`summary_translations`).  Opt-in like `summary`.

title.description:
The language model's title for a finished recording (made by the
same call as the summary).  Opt-in like `summary`; without it the
recording keeps its name.

voice.description:
(`transcript.voice` clips).  Opt-in (2026-10-20): off unless the
request asks for it; the dashboard asks.  Synthesis is still only
paid for languages a listener actually chose.  Off also skips the
English pivot finalize writes for the voice tracks.
voice.title: 48: speak each audience language's translation as it lands

voiceByLang.description:
Which voice speaks each audience language (`{"es": "F3"}`), by the
engine's own voice name or `clone:<id>`.  A language that is not
listed gets the engine's default for it.

This is the host's setting, not a listener's: a clip is
synthesised once per language and fanned out to everyone
listening in it (`relay.rs` filters by language alone), so a
per-listener choice could not be honoured without synthesising
per listener.  The listener's picker therefore offers what is
pinned here — usually the one voice actually being rendered.

SettingsPatch.description:
Partial update (PATCH) — every field optional, `null` for
`spokenLanguage` means back to auto-detect.

voiceByLang.description: Replaces the whole map; `{}` clears every pin.

ShareLink.description:
The broadcast or transcription something belongs to (a script, a share
link): exactly one of `broadcastId` and `transcriptionId` is set.
Flattened into its owner.

broadcastId.description: Set when it belongs to a broadcast.

transcriptionId.description: Set when it belongs to a transcription.

SourceInfo.description:
What the recording was made from (design `j.meta`: "M4A · 34.2 MB",
"Video URL").

durationS.description: Probed media duration, known before the transcript is.

format.description: Upper-case container label ("M4A", "MP4"), from the name or the mime type.

name.description: The file's name, or the URL without its scheme.

SourceProblem.description: What went wrong, as the app explains it.

oneOf.description: The server says there is nothing at that address (HTTP 404 / 410).
The server refused it (401, 403 and other 4xx).
The server is failing (5xx, 429): usually passes.
No such host: the name does not resolve.
The host would not take the connection (refused, TLS, network).
A private or internal address, which the server does not fetch.
It answered, but no audio came within the time allowed.
A web page, not a stream.
A playlist whose entries gave no audio, or that lists none.
Data came back, but not audio that can be decoded.
Audio in a format or with a protection the server does not read.
A YouTube live that has not started yet.
A YouTube video that is not live (a finished broadcast, an upload).
YouTube will not play it (private, removed, region or age locked).
YouTube is turning this server away for now.

SpeakerLabels.description:
The three positions of the speaker-labels switch (design 77), on a
realtime session's options and on a broadcast's, transcription's or
recording's settings alike.

`auto` ("When Needed") diarizes like `on`, and its lines are labelled
only once a second speaker has been heard, so one person talking reads
as plain text.  `on` labels every line; `off` (the default, #39)
neither separates nor labels.

gender.description:
`"male"` / `"female"` once the pitch band settles on this speaker,
absent while it has not or when it refused to judge (§casting).
Absent is "not known" and never "neither": nothing may infer a
gender from its absence.

identified.description:
This speaker is somebody the account holds a voice for.

Said to EVERYONE, unlike `voiceId` below. The mark beside a
speaker's name is about the person — they are not a numbered
cluster, they are somebody who can be read in their own voice —
and a listener is entitled to know that much. Which voice, and
how sure, is the detail they are denied.

Without this the mark depended on `voiceId` or a colour, and a
voice whose owner never chose a colour gave a listener neither:
the speaker was identified and looked exactly like one who was
not.

identifiedConfidence.description:
The match's cosine, when a model made it. Absent when a person
did: nobody guessed.

voiceColor.description:
That voice's colour, so the person reads the same here as
everywhere else.

voiceId.description:
The saved voice this speaker turned out to be — matched by the
engine, or asserted by a host who enrolled them mid-recording
(design 34).

Here as well as on the live frame because the live frame is heard
once: a reader who joins later, or reloads, or opens the
recording next week, learns it only from the snapshot. Without it
the mark beside a speaker's name survived exactly as long as the
socket did.

StartJob.description:
`POST /v1/recordings/{id}/job/start`: the window a job in
`cropping` should transcribe.  Both bounds optional: the start of the
file and its end.

audioSource.description:
On a broadcast: record this one of its audio sources
(`Broadcast.audioSources[].id`) instead of the microphone.

scriptId.description:
Start the recording a script (made in the VocalStack app) was
written for: its text is copied onto the recording and the engine
follows it (`Recording.scriptText`).

scriptText.description:
The words this recording follows (HTML subset: ``, ``, ``, `
`; anything else is reduced to that): the engine matches the transcript against them like a teleprompter. With `scriptId`, the script's own text wins.

settings.description: Overrides for this recording only; its broadcast's or transcription's settings otherwise.

takeover.description: Take the mic from a publisher that is attached elsewhere.

StreamIngest.description:
The server-side publisher of a stream source's recording, on the
`Recording` DTO as `ingest`.

attempts.description: Worker runs so far (1 = never re-claimed).

detected.description: What the stream turned out to be, e.g. `progressive mp3 (audio/mpeg)`.

error.description:
The last thing that went wrong (kept while reconnecting; the reason
once failed).

failures.description: Consecutive failed connects in the current run.

lastAudioAt.description:
When the source last delivered audio, once it has stopped (design
91): a stream that is still connected but silent — an RTMP encoder
that stopped, a YouTube live that ended — is `reconnecting` from
[`STALL_AFTER`] on, with this.

mediaAt.description:
Where the recording's media clock starts in wall-clock time: the
HLS program date-time of the first segment pulled, when the stream
carried one (YouTube does).  Media second `t` of the recording was
broadcast at `media_at + t`.

startedAt.description: When the first audio reached the engine.

streamStartedAt.description:
When the stream behind a YouTube link began, read off the
stream's segment numbering: second 0 of the archive YouTube keeps
once the stream ends.  Media second `t` of the recording is second
`media_at - stream_started_at + t` of that video, which is how a
replay shows the picture at the moment being played.

oneOf.description: Switch target language (a property of this stream).

audio.description: Opt in/out of live original audio.

SubscriberFrame.description:
Frames a subscriber can receive in addition to the engine's
`ServerFrame`s.  Documented in the contract's `x-websocket.subscribe`.

oneOf.description:
First frame after the upgrade: where the live sequence stands, so
the client fetches the snapshot up to `lastSeq` and discards
buffered frames at or below it.
Recording state changed (LIVE ⇄ PAUSED → ENDED → FINALIZED).
Capture settings changed mid-recording (mode, language, labels).
The silence watchdog will pause the recording soon.
The max-duration cutoff is near.
A human correction was applied — distinct from an engine amend.

text.description: The segment's full text after the correction.

wordIdx.description: `-1` for a line rewrite, which carries `words` instead.

words.description:
The segment's full word list whenever the count changed: a line
rewrite, or a word replaced by several words (and the undo of
either). Absent when one word became one word.

oneOf.description:
A speaker's gender, once the pitch band settles on it
(`casting::roster`).  Engine → control; the voice sheet marks a
speaker's chip with it and opens the group of voices that suits
them.  Never used to pick a voice — `voice_cast` does that, on the
engine, where the verdict is made.

A speaker and the saved voice they turn out to be.

Two things produce this and they are the same claim: the engine
matching somebody against a saved voice, and the host enrolling
them from inside the recording (design 34) — the second being the
stronger of the two, since a person said it rather than a model.
Either way the reader learns the same thing: this speaker is that
person, their voice exists, and it is this colour.

An empty `name` withdraws the claim.
A per-recording speaker label.

Broadcast or transcription topic: a recording started in it (it is
live).  `transcriptionId` is the transcription the recording is made
in: on a broadcast's topic, the live transcription feeding it.

A file / URL transcription job moved (both topics: the recording's
and its broadcast's or transcription's).  `state` is the job state; the counts feed the
design's `x / N SEGMENTS`.

fetchedBytes.description:
While `state` is `fetching`: bytes of the source in so far and
the total once known, and the phase — `fetching` or
`extracting` (the audio being taken out of a video).

phasePct.description: How far that phase is, 0..100, when it can be told.

preview.description:
The server holds a fetched link's copy for the trim step to read
(`TranscriptionJob.preview`).

oneOf.description:
A stream source's server-side publisher moved (both topics): what
the server is doing with the URL — connecting, streaming,
reconnecting after a drop, stopped, or failed with `error`.

failures.description: Consecutive failed connects (the retry cadence follows from it).

lastAudioAt.description:
When the source last delivered audio (design 91: "last audio
00:14 ago"), set once it stops.

oneOf.description:
Broadcast or transcription topic: the recording that was live in it
ended (on a broadcast's topic, also: the live transcription making
it was detached).
Admin subscribers: the audience aggregate, every few seconds.
The frame sequence jumped; the client should re-snapshot from its cursor.

cancelReason.description:
Who set the cancel, while it is set: `customer`, or
`interval_withdrawn` (monthly billing is no longer offered on the
plan and the customer has not switched to yearly).

nextPayment.description:
The renewal: on or about when, and how much (the list price of what
it renews on, tax included or added as the customer's country
requires); null when it ends at the period end.

pastDueSince.description: When the renewal first failed (the provider retries on its own).

pendingInterval.description: A switch to the other interval scheduled for the period end.

returnPlan.description: The plan the account returns to when this subscription ends.

scheduledEnd.description:
An end already scheduled, other than the customer's own cancel: by
us (`our_choice`, Terms section 18, with at least 30 days' notice) or
at the customer's request when the Terms change (`section_22`); null
otherwise.

switchPrices.description:
What a switch to each interval charges per period (the version the
next renewal is on), null where not offered: the `expectedPrice` of
`POST /v1/billing/subscription/interval` and the yearly opt-in.

yearlyOptIn.description:
Monthly billing is no longer offered and the subscription ends at its
renewal unless the customer switches to yearly
(`POST /v1/billing/subscription/yearly-opt-in`); an uncancel is
refused (`409 invalid_state`) while this is true.

SummaryStatus.description: Where a recording's summary stands, for `POST /v1/recordings/:id/summarize`.

lang.description:
The language the title and summary read in when they were asked
for in one (`GET .../summary?lang=`) and could be translated into
it; absent, they read as spoken.

state.description:
`ready`: the recording carries a title and summary.  `pending`: the
pass is queued or running; read the recording again shortly.
`unavailable`: this server has no summariser configured.
`not_requested`: the recording was made without `summary` (or is
shorter than a minute, which never gets one); `POST .../summarize`
asks for it.

month.description: Dollars (USD), a decimal number with at most six decimals.

year.description: Dollars (USD), a decimal number with at most six decimals.

TagRef.description: A tag as a transcription lists it.

TagTranscriptions.description: Transcriptions to put the tag on and to take it off, by id.

lang.description: The language translations were filtered to, when one was asked for.

lastSeq.description: Every frame at or below this is reflected in the snapshot.

speakerLabels.description:
How this recording labels its speakers (design 77): `on` names
every line's speaker, `off` none, `auto` only once a second speaker
has been heard.  A reader with no settings to look at — a listener,
a share link — follows this.

Transcription.description:
A transcription: a file, a link (with its `transcription` job), or
something captured as it is spoken (`live: true`: a microphone, a
stream, an RTMP encoder), which may feed broadcasts (`broadcasts`).

batchId.description:
The batch this file was sent in (`POST /v1/batches`); absent for a
transcription made on its own.  A batch's files are listed by the
batch (`GET /v1/batches/{id}`), not by `transcriptions.list`.

broadcasts.description: The broadcasts a live transcription feeds.

createdByApiKeyId.description:
The API key that created it, when it was created with one (through
the API, not in the web app); absent otherwise, and once that key
has been deleted.

currentRecording.description: The recording in flight, if one is.

job.description: A file or link transcription's job: state, progress, source.

kind.description: Always `transcription`: which resource this is, for a client holding both.

lastRecording.description: A live transcription's newest recording, once it has one.

live.description:
Captured live (a microphone or a stream) rather than read from a
file or a link: it has recordings to start and stop, no job, and
can feed broadcasts.

origin.description:
Where it was made: `dashboard` (the web app), `api` (an API key),
one of our apps (`extension`, `desktop_app`, `obs`, `wordpress`,
`payload`, `strapi`, `contentful`), `mcp`, `batch_api`, a broadcast's
encoder (`broadcast`), or `unknown`.

source.description:
A live transcription's microphone, or the stream URL the server
pulls; a file or link transcription says `mic` (its source is the
job's).

tags.description: The account's tags on it, by name (`tags.list`).

crop.description: The window transcribed, chosen in the crop step; absent = the whole file.

errorCode.description:
Why a `failed` job failed, when it is machine-readable:
`insufficient_credit` — the source, once its length was known, cost
more than the owner's credit; `usage_cap_reached` — more than the
API key that made it has left of its usage cap.  Neither is retried
on its own: retry once credit is added or the cap allows it.
`stopped` — stopped by its owner (`POST /v1/recordings/{id}/stop`);
what was transcribed before the stop is kept.

info.description:
Speech to text, live translation and spoken translations, as one API.

## What is what

- **Realtime session**: a stateless token for one WebSocket. `POST /v1/realtime/sessions` returns a signed `streamUrl`; nothing is stored. Audio goes in as binary frames and transcript events come out (`x-websocket.realtimeSession`). The API uses the word for nothing else.
- **Transcription**: a stored transcript of a file, a link, or something captured as it is spoken (a microphone, a stream, an RTMP encoder: `live: true`). `POST /v1/transcriptions` (a file or a link) and `POST /v1/transcriptions/live`.
- **Broadcast**: the link listeners open (`code`). It is fed by the live transcriptions attached to it, or records one of its own audio sources. `POST /v1/broadcasts`.
- **Recording**: one take, always inside a transcription (`transcriptionId`); a recording started on a broadcast is made in a live transcription attached to it. Its transcript, audio, translations, voice and summary hang off `/v1/recordings/{id}`.
- **Job**: the server's work on a file or link recording: `GET /v1/recordings/{id}/job`.

Hosts authenticate with an API key (`vs_key_…`) or a signed-in person's access token: `Authorization: Bearer …`. Listeners authenticate with nothing (a public broadcast), a share link's code (`shareCode=`, from `transcriptions.createShareLink` or `broadcasts.createShareLink`), or the listener token VocalStack's own listener page holds for a private broadcast (`listenerToken=`). Each operation names its auth mode and key scopes in `x-vocalstack-auth` and `x-vocalstack-scopes`. Every operation is open to every plan: a transcription spends the account's credit per second of audio, and at least the plan's minimum once (`rates.minimumSeconds` on `GET /v1/billing`: a file shorter than the minimum is billed the minimum, a longer one its length; a live transcription stopped and started again is still one transcription; a realtime session is one of its own; a batch of files pays one minimum between its files, each file at least `rates.batchFileMinimumSeconds`), and a creation without that much credit is refused `402 insufficient_credit`.

## Streaming in 30 seconds

1. `POST /v1/realtime/sessions` → `{ sessionId, streamUrl, expiresAt }`. `streamUrl` embeds a signed token; `expiresAt` is a connect-by deadline only.
2. Open a WebSocket to `streamUrl`. You may receive `session.loading` heartbeats while a cold machine spins up; wait for `session.ready`.
3. Send binary frames of raw PCM (`pcm_f32le`, 16 kHz, mono — exactly `capabilities.audio`). To transcribe a **file** instead, create the realtime session with `input: { kind: "file" }` and send the file's own bytes (mp3, wav, flac, ogg, m4a…) — the server decodes it and transcribes at full speed, reporting `transcript.progress` as it goes.
4. Receive `transcript.committed` (immutable, gapless `seq`, always includes word timings), `transcript.draft` (**full replacement** of the live tail — never append drafts), and `transcript.words` frames.
5. At any time, send `{"type":"session.update", ...}` to change the `latencyMode`, `spokenLanguage`, `speakerLabels` and/or `translate` languages mid-stream; omitted fields are unchanged and already-delivered transcript is not re-translated.
6. Send `{"type":"eof"}` at end of source; the server flushes final commits, sends `session.done`, and closes.

There is no resume: a dropped connection ends the realtime session — reconnect = create a new one. A saturated fleet surfaces as a hanging connect or a bare 503, not an error envelope; clients synthesize `capacity_exceeded` from a connect/ready deadline (the SDKs default to 30 s).

## Stored transcriptions and broadcasts

**Publishing:** `POST /v1/transcriptions/{id}/recordings` (or `/v1/broadcasts/{id}/recordings`) → a `streamUrl`; connect and send PCM exactly as on a realtime session. Control (pause/resume/stop/settings) is HTTP, never in-band. A live transcription whose source is a stream URL has no microphone behind it: the server opens the URL when recording starts and publishes it itself; the grant then has no `streamUrl`, and `recording.ingest` and the `stream.ingest` frame report `connecting` → `streaming` → `reconnecting` → `stopped` | `failed`.

**Listening:** `WS /v1/recordings/{id}/subscribe?lang=es[&voice=F3][&listenerToken=…]` → first frame `subscribe.ready {lastSeq}`; then `GET /v1/recordings/{id}/transcript?lang=es` and discard buffered frames with `seq <= lastSeq`. Every durable frame carries a gapless `seq`; on a jump, re-snapshot with `after=<cursor>` (`x-websocket.subscribe`). `WS /v1/broadcasts/{id}/events` tells a waiting listener when the broadcast goes live, and `WS /v1/events` tells an owner's dashboard when its lists changed.

## Headers

Every response carries `X-Request-Id` (also `requestId` in an error body): what support asks for. Send your own and it is kept. Rate-limited operations answer with `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`: slow down before the `429`. A `429 rate_limited` and a `503 unavailable` carry `Retry-After`, the seconds to wait before sending the request again. What to retry and how: [Errors, retries and limits](/docs/guides/errors-and-limits.md).

accountEvents.description: The owner's dashboard: `events.ready` once the socket is listening, then `lists.changed` whenever a list of transcriptions or broadcasts of any principal the caller may act for is out of date — a recording changed state, a transcription settled, a title was written, or the owner changed something from another device. It says that, not what: re-read `GET /v1/transcriptions` and `GET /v1/broadcasts`. It replaces polling those lists. A user may hold a few of these at once (5 by default): opening one more closes their oldest with code 4001. One is closed with code 4002 after a day. After either, do not reconnect at once — a client that does takes its place straight back; reconnect when the user next uses that screen.
accountEvents.query: access_token (a browser cannot set a header on a socket)

broadcastEvents.description: What a screen waiting on a broadcast needs: when a recording starts in it (`recording.started`: it is live), when that recording ends (`recording.ended`), a file job's progress (`job.progress`), and a pulled stream's state (`stream.ingest`). Each frame's `transcriptionId` is the transcription the recording is made in: on a broadcast's socket, the live transcription feeding it.
broadcastEvents.query: listenerToken / shareCode / access_token, as on subscribe

connectErrors.description: Rejected upgrades carry the ApiErrorBody envelope over HTTP.

realtimeSession.description: Connect to the `streamUrl` a realtime session returned (treat it as opaque).
rules: transcript.draft is a FULL REPLACEMENT of the live tail (replace-not-append)
segment.seq is per realtime session, monotonic, 0-based, gapless; ordering only
single total order per realtime session; the draft tail begins at the last committed segment's end
committed segments always include words; their text/speaker may later be corrected by a transcript.amended frame (same seq) — apply it in place
sentences.enabled: transcript.sentence is a FULL REPLACEMENT upsert keyed by sentenceId (status open -> closed; dropped = discard); seqs lists the committed segments it covers
sentences.enabled + translate: translations attach to transcript.sentence (provisional=true while open, replaced on close) instead of transcript.translated
events.drafts / events.words govern live frames only
clients MUST ignore unknown server frame types; servers ignore unknown client text frames
no resume: a dropped connection ends the realtime session; reconnect = create a new one
backpressure: commits are never dropped; drafts/words coalesce-latest; slow consumers are closed with slow_consumer
saturation may surface OUTSIDE this envelope as a hanging connect or bare 503 from the load balancer; clients synthesize capacity_exceeded from a connect/ready deadline
file input (input.kind=file): binary frames carry the encoded file; transcription starts at eof, so no transcript frames arrive before it

file input emits transcript.progress on a timer (also the keep-alive); maxDurationS applies to the file's DECODED duration — a longer-than-allowed file is refused with invalid_audio, or truncated with session.done/max_duration when the container declared no duration
file input defaults events.drafts to false (a draft previews a live tail that a file does not have); ask explicitly to receive them

session.done carries stats {audioS, processingS, realtimeFactor} measured server-side; processingS excludes a file's upload and decode setup, and the object is the extension point for future metadata about the realtime session

subscribe.binary: Ogg/Opus pages of the original audio, only after subscribe.update{audio:true}; droppable under backpressure
subscribe.description: Follow a recording: first frame `subscribe.ready {lastSeq}`, then `GET /v1/recordings/{id}/transcript` and discard buffered frames with `seq <= lastSeq`. `voice` picks which voice speaks the language for this listener; two listeners on the same (lang, voice) share one synthesis, so changing voice means reopening the socket. Send `{"type":"subscribe.update","lang":"ja"}` to switch language, `{"type":"subscribe.update","audio":true}` to receive live Opus.
subscribe.query: lang (translation target — through a share link it needs the link's allowTranslate, else the upgrade is refused 403 and a mid-socket subscribe.update{lang} closes the socket with 1008), voice (which voice speaks it — a voice id from GET /v1/voices/available?lang=…; omit for the recording's settings.voiceByLang pin, else the engine's default), listenerToken / shareCode / access_token, role, device
rules: durable frames carry seq (gapless per recording); ephemeral frames (transcript.words, audio.chunk) carry none; recordings emit no transcript.draft
a frame withheld from a role still consumes its seq: listeners receive {type:'noop', seq} in its place, so a real jump always means a missed frame
listeners receive translations filtered to their lang; suppressed lines arrive with text='' and suppressed=true

transcript.voice is filtered to the listener's (lang, voice): a clip reaches only subscribers whose voice= matches its voiceKey (both empty = the engine's default), and one clip serves every listener on that pair — the voice is chosen per listener, the synthesis is paid once

a long line is spoken in pieces (part, parts): the engine cuts it at its clause boundaries so the first piece can be heard while the rest are still being made. The pieces share the sentence id, arrive in order, and are played back to back — one line on screen, with one translation and one place in the reading. part=0/parts=1 is a line spoken whole

transcript.voiceStatus is filtered to the same (lang, voice) pair as transcript.voice: state 'preparing' means that voice's assets are downloading and the sentences spoken meanwhile are held and will arrive as clips; 'unavailable' means it cannot be spoken here and detail says why. A listener never hears a different voice than the one asked for
admin subscribers (owning-principal members) receive the full frame set plus audience aggregates
recording.state announces LIVE ⇄ PAUSED → ENDED → FINALIZED; listeners are not disconnected at ENDED
transcript.corrected is a human edit; transcript.amended is an engine rewrite — clients clear uncertainty marks only on the former
